Maintenance audit — 31 October to 2 November 2026

Source: MAINTENANCE.md

Hosted graphics follow-up — 3 November 2026

Published commit 68f01fb failed the macOS job of run 41604932875: R’s SVG device could not load the X11 library used by Cairo, and no SVG file was created. The existing shared workflow’s macos-xquartz input is now enabled; the test is retained and the native prerequisite is documented in the README and export help.

An independent failure probe also confirmed that the exporter printed “Figure saved” even when the device wrote nothing. Exports now render to a temporary file in the target directory and require nonempty output before publication. A previous output is preserved before replacement and restored after a failed move. If restoration itself fails, the backup remains and its location is reported. Device warnings remain visible.

A warning-only SVG initialization failure could additionally let ggplot2 draw on the caller’s current device or open a default PDF. The SVG device wrapper now checks that initialization actually opened a new device before drawing starts. An actual-ggsave regression preserves an owned caller device; an independent fresh-R probe confirms that the default device is not opened and no unintended PDF is created. Guarded SVG dimensions match the original native device exactly; on this R build Cairo expresses dimensions as integer points.

All 581 local assertions pass without warnings or skips, including 48 new assertions for missing/empty/partial output, rollback and retained backups, device ownership and real PDF/PNG/SVG/TIFF/EPS file signatures. Workflow syntax validation passes. House lint remains report-only: 62 findings versus 59 on the base, with the three additions deliberately signaling native-style warnings and an error in failure fixtures. No lint policy or test coverage was weakened. Exact archive checks and subsequent hosted results are recorded separately.

The original Ubuntu oldrel-3 job did not reach package tests: its optional survminer dependency chain ended at Deriv requiring R >= 4.5. That pre-existing informational row and its dependency-resolution evidence remain visible. This follow-up does not claim that oldrel-3 or a CRAN release is qualified, and it does not resolve the separately documented maintainer-contact or publication gates.

Repository: CTTIR/dynasimR. Base: 076a99c0281cb199670c40759b514956bb005ef7. Work is isolated from the clean original checkout. No publication or submission is authorized by this maintenance record.

Purpose and baseline

The package promises a common analysis API for two simulation-output profiles, a Shiny dashboard and publication exports. The important user paths are loading one’s own files, obtaining faithful descriptive/survival/policy results, selecting the same data across dashboard analyses, and exporting usable plots, tables and manuscript values without modifying the source manuscript.

On R 4.6.1 the unmodified source passed 217 assertions in 142 test blocks, with no failures or skips and four ggplot2 deprecation warnings. fresh and survminer were absent from the initial library; this is an environment fact, not a package defect. Existing hosted checks passed on the base commit; maintenance-branch CI has not run. A real browser baseline rendered all seven tabs without visible/JavaScript errors and downloaded a valid 42,613-byte PDF. This does not establish correctness of custom-data or hostile-input paths. Raw baseline and independent probe evidence is retained in the workspace audit under evidence/dynasimR/.

Milestones

  1. Faithful inputs and scientific results. Repair the confirmed input and statistical defects with regression fixtures derived independently of the implementation. Preserve original example/source data. Both profiles must retain their documented units and meaning. Do not silently substitute a different model or treat a dropped observation as fitted.
  2. Usable dashboard and exports. Keep selection consistent across analyses, treat scenario IDs and table cells as data, preserve source manuscripts, and exercise actual application startup, tabs and downloads. Compile and inspect exported LaTeX rather than relying only on string assertions.
  3. Dependable maintenance and release package. Repair portable developer checks, update implementation/docs/tests together, resolve deprecations, build vignettes and a source archive, install into a fresh project library, and run the applicable package checks. Record actual external-release status.
  4. Independent review and handover. Challenge corrected results and failure paths, verify source/archive correspondence and sole Git identity, retain evidence and give exact first-use commands. Complete all unblocked repairs.

Dependencies: statistical/input contracts precede final dashboard and report qualification; final documentation and packaging follow completed source edits. The strongest coherent release preserves supported analysis meaning and makes failures explicit. A new simulation engine, speculative architectural rewrite, full Morris trajectory redesign, additional dashboard features and scientific validation of users’ simulation models remain outside this maintenance scope.

Release evidence and gates

Rechecked on 2 November 2026: the CRAN package index has no dynasimR entry. The public Zenodo record and DataCite DOI endpoints return 404 for 10.5281/zenodo.21889932; the existing .zenodo.json explicitly says the record is a prepared, unpublished draft. Preserve that draft identifier and author/ORCID provenance without presenting it as confirmed public publication. Do not submit or publish automatically.

The placeholder r-heller@example.org cannot serve as the reachable maintainer contact required by CRAN policy. A preferred public contact has been requested; independent implementation and validation continue while that metadata remains unresolved.

Work and verification

Completed implementation

  • Inputs are validated per file before binding, with explicit scenario identity, complete file pairs and ownership of caller metadata. All 18 original files under data-raw, data and inst/extdata match the base SHA-256 values.
  • Statistical repairs cover signed policy results, unequal-sample effect sizes, coherent bootstrap intervals, invalid/censored inputs, fitted sample counts, literal model predictors, binary outcome labels and autonomy reduction bands. A nondefault autonomy reference is now labelled correctly in the plot.
  • Survival plots include time zero, genuine numbers at risk and visible singleton-time estimates. Progress ranges are labelled as descriptive. Cost-outcome plots retain their fixed-reference estimator with honest observed fraction labels; undefined ratios no longer acquire an arbitrary epsilon.
  • Manuscript exports treat identifiers as data, protect source/output files, reject requested unknown/unavailable results, and escape literal LaTeX text. Real PDF/PNG/SVG and table exports were exercised, compiled where applicable, and visually inspected.
  • Dashboard selection is consistent across KM/Cox. Profile B has supported overview/comparison/summary export and explicit messages for unavailable analyses. Mixed-profile dashboard input fails clearly; the R loader remains available for mixed data. Hostile-looking identifiers do not execute code.
  • Portable developer scripts replace machine-specific paths and obsolete APIs. Documentation regeneration retains unrelated files; the release check fails on notes as well as errors/warnings. Developer negative fixtures confirm undeclared namespaces and a wrong documentation-generator version exit 1.
  • Version 0.1.1 is prepared as an unpublished development candidate. Citation metadata retains the original author/ORCID. Repository-only metadata and the linked-worktree .git file are excluded from source distributions.

Observed verification

  • Baseline: 217 assertions, four deprecation warnings. Intermediate integrated source tests: 495 assertions, no warnings/failures/skips. Subsequent focused tests cover completion models, cost outcomes and plot edge cases.
  • First complete R CMD check --as-cran: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 4 notes; 532 assertions passed with one existing skip_on_cran resource test. Vignette rebuilds and PDF/HTML manuals passed. Three notes identified stray repository metadata; exclusions were repaired. The remaining incoming note says new submission and displays the current placeholder maintainer.
  • Final R CMD check --as-cran: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 1 note, with 532 assertions passed and one existing CRAN-specific skip. All vignette rebuilds and PDF/HTML manuals passed. The remaining note is the new-submission incoming check displaying the placeholder maintainer. The strict developer script exits 1 for this note; it has not passed the final release gate.
  • Full source browser journeys for both profiles passed with real downloads. A fresh-library installed app also started and downloaded a valid PDF. No browser JavaScript errors or injected identifiers were observed.
  • The local pkgdown site built; seven principal pages passed browser checks, including local links/images and desktop/mobile visual inspection. This is local site evidence, not deployment to GitHub Pages.
  • The final source archive contains no .git, .zenodo.json, CITATION.cff, Rplots.pdf or .checks content. Its 180 comparable source files match the worktree. The source-data manifest verifies all 18 original data files.

Detailed logs, test results, screenshots, rendered files and SHA-256 manifests are retained in the workspace audit’s evidence/dynasimR/. Original failed attempts are retained separately from successful follow-up runs.

First use

For a new installation, R >= 4.1 is required. From the repository checkout:

install.packages(c("remotes", "xtable", "shiny", "shinydashboard",
                   "shinyWidgets", "plotly", "DT"))
remotes::install_local(".", dependencies = NA, upgrade = "never")
library(dynasimR)
sim <- load_example_data()
print(policy_effect(sim, "A-S08", "A-S07"))
plot_km(km_estimate(sim, endpoint = "stage2"))
launch_app()  # http://127.0.0.1:3838; stop with Ctrl-C in the R console

Use read_simulation("/path/to/outputs") for your files. Profile B analyses are listed in README; mixed-profile directories must be separated for the dashboard. LaTeX compilation requires the preamble described in the manuscript vignette. The source-package check additionally needs Pandoc, TeX, rcmdcheck and roxygen2 8.0.0. Rscript dev/smoke_test.R exercises both profiles; use Rscript dev/doc_and_check.R for the strict source-package release gate.

Remaining gates and deferred work

Local scientific/input/export defects identified by this audit are repaired. Scientific qualification of a user’s simulation model and dependence structure is outside this package audit. Entity-level bootstrap intervals assume independence; matched runs and replication clustering require an appropriate study-specific method. Morris trajectory designs and inferential economic acceptability analysis remain outside this release.

Before submission: supply an approved reachable maintainer email, review the CRAN incoming note, rerun checks for the exact release commit on Linux/Windows and supported R versions, and confirm the intended archival record. Shared hosted lint/coverage are currently report-only and hosted R checks omit the PDF manual; those are not substitutes for this local manual/check evidence.

The original checkout remains clean at the base commit. Maintenance changes are isolated on maintenance/public-readiness-20261030 and use the verified R. Heller author and committer identity. Nothing was pushed, submitted, merged, deployed or published. The next publication action is maintainer review of these commits and metadata, followed by authorized hosted checks and release.

Final archive: .checks/20261102-161658/dynasimR_0.1.1.tar.gz (1,717,274 bytes). SHA-256: 571c7c719dad3b710deac203352a28a173f67095b4f877227aaf14fa1b769303. The final check includes CRAN incoming checks and did not disable manual checks. Actionlint passed all four local workflow files. No hosted workflow was run for these maintenance commits.

The exact final archive installed successfully into a fresh project library. A new R process verified that library’s namespace, loaded 16,000 example entities and 200 replication summaries, and passed the installed-package smoke workflow for both profiles and real PDF/LaTeX exports. Existing dependency libraries were reused; this was not a clean operating-system/dependency installation. The installed browser smoke preceded the final documentation/packaging-only rebuild; the app source is identical in both archives.
